$comment: Downward-only ratchets for the three published claims whose measured floor sits above their original <= 1 bar. D-102 says why the floor is structural and D-148 records the shrink to 24,202 B; on 2026-09-27 the owner decided (D-157) that each becomes 'something acceptable and realistic, while we consistently keep them as low as we can': a ceiling just above today's measurement, gated on every run, that may only ever be lowered. `ceiling` is the one number `benchmarks/claims.ts` and the B2/B4 gates read (`benchmarks/claim-ratchets.ts`). `history` is append-only and never rises: `scripts/claim-ratchets-lock.test.ts` refuses a `ceiling` that is not the last entry, an entry above the one before it unless it cites a newer D-row that exists in .sdlc/DECISIONS.md, and a history that rewrites the committed one. `npm run ratchets:propose` prints the lower ceiling each can move to from the latest measurement, by the `derive` rule written beside it.

cold-start-at-or-below-cac.was: <= 1: burgee starts at or below cac, the lightest framework in the landscape

derive.rule: The median `burgee ÷ cac` cold-start ratio of the last 26 CI observations in benchmarks/results/cli-benchmarks/*-ci.json (2026-10-09 8d601e7 to 2026-10-11 42b60dc, every one a descendant of #898, which took node:util and node:fs off the start-up path): mean 1.424, sd 0.033, p95 1.461, max 1.463. The larger of mean + 3 sd (1.523) and the max, rounded up to the next 0.05: 1.55. The first ceiling, 1.6, came from the 26 runs 2026-09-22 c0fa8a3 to 2026-09-27 7b694f7 (mean 1.490, sd 0.034, max 1.553), where the p95 rounded up would have been 1.55 and c938fbf's 1.553 sat above it: one run in 26 red for nothing, the flake #27 already made twice. Absolute milliseconds are the runner's; the ratio of two interleaved spawns is what the gate reads.

history.why: First ceiling. Replaces B2's `burgee` gate of 1.7 and the claim's <= 1. Measured 1.512 on the newest CI observation (7b694f7).

Lowered after #898 (8d601e7) took the node:util and node:fs namespaces off burgee's start-up path. The 26 CI observations since it merged average 1.424 against 1.490 for the 26 that set 1.6, and none exceeds 1.463. Mean + 3 sd is 1.523, rounded up to 1.55; lowering by 1/1.25 of the 0.066 fall gives 1.547, the same step. Measured 1.363 on the newest CI observation (42b60dc).

lighter-than-commander.was: <= 1: burgee/commander is lighter in a user's bundle than commander alone

derive.rule: Bundle ratios are deterministic, so this is the build's own measurement: burgee/commander 55,346 B over commander's 39,084 B = 1.416, and CI reads the same 55,346 B (1.416) at every reading from 2026-10-13-ba91416-ci through 2026-10-19-c05c86e-ci. CI has measured about 32 B heavier than a local build elsewhere, so 80 B go on our side before rounding: 55,426 / 39,084 = 1.418, rounded up to the next 0.005 (the step this row's B4 ceiling has moved in since D-100) is 1.42, which holds 55,499 B. B4's byte ceiling for burgee/commander (55,400) still binds first; this is the ceiling on the published ratio. The first ceiling, 1.565, was 60,969 B over 39,084 B at 7b694f7, before commander-front-end-diet took 5,623 B off.

history.why: First ceiling, and B4's `burgee/commander` ratio ceiling from J3/J4 (2026-09-24) carried over, not raised. Replaces the claim's <= 1.

Lowered after commander-front-end-diet R1 and R2 (bellpull behind import(), the completion and --mcp routers in a lazily loaded commander/surfaces.js) took burgee/commander from 60,969 B to 55,346 B. Every CI reading since 2026-10-13-ba91416-ci is 55,346 B, ratio 1.416. (55,346 + 80) / 39,084 = 1.418, rounded up to 0.005, is 1.42.

lighter-than-cac.was: <= 1: burgee is lighter in a user's bundle than cac alone

derive.rule: Bundle ratios are deterministic, so this is the build's own measurement on main after #631: burgee 24,216 B over cac's 10,452 B = 2.317. CI measures about 32 B heavier than a local build, so 80 B go on our side before rounding: 24,296 / 10,452 = 2.324, rounded up to the next 0.05 is 2.35, which holds 24,562 B. B4's byte ceiling (24,500 since D-20261019-typed-schema-surface-weight) still binds first; this is the ceiling on the published ratio.

history.why: First ceiling. Replaces the claim's <= 1, and binds B4's `burgee ÷ cac` gate below the wave-5 release budget of 2.9, which stays the release's outer limit.
